headline: Rangers’ Alberts Smits out week-to-week with upper-body injury
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Rangers defenseman Alberts Smits is out week-to-week with an upper-body injury. Smits made the team out of camp as the No. 5 overall pick in June's draft and has yet to record his first NHL point, per Daily Faceoff.

The numbers say the missing point is partly bad luck. Over 17 games so far this season, Smits has put up 0.88 expected goals (a measure of the quality of his shot chances) and scored none, so his results trail his chances by 0.88 goals. At 5-on-5 the Rangers have taken 47.9% of the expected goals with him on the ice, and the team's share runs about six points better with him off it, so he has been a mild drag, which is fair for an 18-year-old third-pair defenseman playing 14:35 a night. The Rangers are 10-7-1 and hold 53% of expected goals overall, so this is a depth loss, not a hit to their strength. On the ice, Matthew Robertson has moved in beside Morrow in the one game since Smits went out, and he is the player to watch for those third-pair minutes.
